subject: Post-discovery recap: schedule dedicated throughput sizing + demo pairing
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finbot.ai>; Elena Zhou <elena.zhou@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery recap: schedule dedicated throughput sizing + demo pairing

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock in the dedicated-capacity sizing work: 

Summary (from our discovery)
- Primary latency target: 95th percentile <= 180ms for short chat prompts (<=512 tokens)
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 12 qps during peak windows, occasional spikes to ~30 qps for 2–5 minutes
- Typical request size: 200–800 tokens; bursty batch of ~1000 requests during batch jobs
- Data sensitivity: PII-in-requests; FinBot prefers Private/VPC deployment or Dedicated with strict retention controls

Next step: schedule a 60–75 minute sizing + technical deep-dive where we:
1) walk your infra/product/ML ops through the throughput profile and SLAs
2) run a quick capacity calcs exercise and alignment on target GPU pool size (we'll bring our Dedicated sizing playbook)
3) pair this with a short demo of runtime controls (batching, prefix caching, routing policies)

Proposed times (PST):
- Thu Jul 1, 10:00–11:15am
- Thu Jul 1, 2:30–3:45pm
- Fri Jul 2, 9:30–10:45am

For the call, could you invite: a technical lead (ML infra or SRE), a product owner who can speak to QPS/SLAs, and anyone from procurement if you want to run timeline/contract questions?

Prep items (we can help):
- Small sample request log or synthetic load profile (CSV) — attach to reply
- Any model variant preference (open model name / family)

I'll put tentative holds on the first two slots and we can cancel the one that doesn't work. Ben (cc) will join the call to run the sizing exercise.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finbot.ai>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery recap: schedule dedicated throughput sizing + demo pairing

Grace — thanks for the clear recap. Both Elena and I are available for the Thu Jul 1 afternoon slot (2:30pm PST). We'll invite:
- Ajit Rao (SRE, ajit.rao@finbot.ai)
- Priya Menon (Product, priya.menon@finbot.ai)

A couple of clarifications before the call so we make the sizing exercise efficient:
1) For bursts, those are originating mostly from our batch ingestion pipeline (not user-facing). Those can be staged to a different routing policy if needed; we'll share a sample event profile.
2) We'd prefer to avoid Private/on-prem right now — Dedicated with encrypted volumes is our likely path.
3) Procurement may want a short-term MSA; looped them in if you want preliminary contract timeline notes.

Attaching a small extract from last week's request log (anonymized).

-- Attachment: finbot_sample_load_profile.csv (CSV, 12KB) --

See you Thursday 2:30. Can you share a calendar invite with a conference bridge (and a link to any pre-read)?

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Engineering, FinBot

On Thu, Jun 30, 2027 at 11:05 AM Samir Patel <samir.patel@finbot.ai> wrote:
> Attaching a small extract from last week's request log (anonymized).

Thanks Samir — received. Grace, quick internal notes before I run the sizing exercise:
- I'll prepare two sizing scenarios: (A) conservative with headroom for 2x bursts, (B) cost-optimized with autoscale and overflow routing to a cheaper variant.
- Please confirm whether FinBot uses mostly 8K-context models or smaller — the CSV shows tokens but not model context. If we assume 4k context for calculations that's fine, but I want to make the assumption explicit in the call.
- I'll also include a short one-page pre-read (attached) that lists the inputs we'll need live on the call so Samir/Ajit can answer quickly.

Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Agenda (45–75 min):
- 5m quick intros and objective alignment
- 25–35m sizing exercise (Ben leads) — live calcs based on the sample log you shared
